capabilities.label: Firecrawl-First Web Routing
capabilities.summary: Route public reading and extraction to local Firecrawl; reserve an authorized per-client browser lane for interactive UI work.
capabilities.outputs: Selected web lane, readiness requirement, and bounded fallback rule.
capabilities.cost_per_call: local Firecrawl or existing browser runtime
capabilities.rate_limit: Two failed attempts per selected lane before diagnostic stop

routing_policy.public_read: Use web_extract backed by FIRECRAWL_API_URL; local Firecrawl is the default.
routing_policy.interactive: Use the existing per-client browser harness for clicks, typing, authentication, uploads, downloads, and UI screenshots. The lane may use a dedicated profile or a personal profile authorized by its principal.
routing_policy.authorization: A clear client instruction to use their browser, existing login, or saved-password autofill is sufficient for the requested scope. If a suitable signed-in personal profile is discovered without clear authorization, identify it without exposing credentials and ask once whether to use it.
routing_policy.credential_use: Within the authorized scope, existing sessions, saved-password autofill, and ordinary login submission are allowed. Never reveal, export, transcribe, log, or move a credential to another surface; human-present factors and consequential-action controls remain in force.
routing_policy.specialized: Prefer an existing tested domain harness for a known brittle workflow; do not create a generic Playwright wrapper.
routing_policy.isolation: Per-client is the ownership boundary: browser profiles, credentials, cookies, tabs, and CDP endpoints must never be shared across principals.
routing_policy.failure_budget: After two failed attempts on the selected lane, stop and return a diagnostic; do not spawn another browser, profile, or daemon.
routing_policy.closeout: Reuse tabs where possible and close task-created tabs when the task ends.
